chunks: Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام, asking him about one who has fallen unconscious for a day or more: should he make up the prayers (salat) that he missed, or not?
So he wrote: “He does not make up the fasting (sawm), nor does he make up the prayer (salat).”

key_terms.الصَّلَوَاتِ: the prescribed prayers that were missed
key_terms.الْمُغْمَى: a person who has lost consciousness
key_terms.يَقْضِي: to make up a missed religious obligation
key_terms.يَوْمًا: a day, indicating the duration of unconsciousness

ai.seo_question: Does an unconscious person have to make up missed prayers and fasting (sawm)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who was unconscious for a day or more. The ruling states that such a person does not have to make up either the missed fasting (sawm) or the missed prayers (salat), indicating lifted liability during unconsciousness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1041 - Ayoub ibn Noah wrote to Abu Al-Hasan al-Third (Imam Musa al-Kadhim) (as) asking whether a person who is unconscious for a day or more needs to make up the prayers (salat) they missed.
The Imam wrote in response, "He does not have to make up the fasting (sawm) or the prayers (salat)."
